messages:
PagerBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: continuous-batching controller reported sustained token latency > 1500ms and elevated 5xx rate on deployed pool 'dedicated-us-west1-a'. Trigger: latency_threshold (3m).

Ada (on-call): Acked. Paging Eli and Morgan. Assigning triage. I'm pulling initial traces and perf counters now.

Eli: I'm on call. Fetching controller logs and kv-cache metrics. First glance: rapid KV cache evictions and spikes in microbatch queue length.

Morgan: Noted. Any customer-facing errors? CustomerOps, can you surface affected workspace list?

CustomerOps: Two customers under Dedicated Tier (acme-analytics, finview) reporting timeouts and 5xx. We have two support tickets created. SLA alert on Acme job churn.

Ada (on-call): Ok. High-level plan: (1) short-term live mitigation to reduce latency/5xx for affected pools, (2) gather root-cause signals (KV cache blowup vs batching jitter), (3) apply hotfix if needed.

Eli: Logs:
```
controller: continuous_batch_wait=1200ms queue_depth=512 microbatch_size=128 kv_cache_entries=12m eviction_rate=high
runtime: transform_latency=950ms token_emit=ms burst_errors=502
```
Seems like microbatch_size jumped to 128 on that pool, and queue_depth climbed with nearly no jitter smoothing. KV cache eviction rate correlates with batch cliff.

Zoe: History check — did we just push the autoscaler rollout/packing policy? DeployBot, any recent deploys to dedicated-us-west1-a?

DeployBot: Deploy 2599999999 by infra/auto-rollout: continuous-batching-controller v1.14.2 -> v1.15.0 rolled to dedicated-us-west1-a at 2604998000. Canary passed 10m.

Morgan: That matches timeframe. v1.15.0 introduced default max_microbatch_size=128 for throughput improvements. Looks like at high concurrency that increased batch wait and caused KV thrash.

Ada (on-call): Live mitigation suggestion: reduce max_microbatch_size for that pool to 32 and enable batch_jitter_smoothing=on. Also cap queue_depth to 256. We should do changes via runtime config patch so it takes effect immediately. Anyone object?

Eli: +1. Also recommend immediate eviction of stale KV entries to free memory and reduce eviction churn: run kvcache-compact on target nodes.

SRE-Triage: Preparing runbook steps. Will coordinate with infra to run the following commands against the pool: 
```
# reduce microbatch size
redwoodctl config set --pool dedicated-us-west1-a --continuous-batching.max_microbatch_size 32
redwoodctl config set --pool dedicated-us-west1-a --continuous-batching.jitter_smoothing true
redwoodctl config set --pool dedicated-us-west1-a --queue.max_depth 256
# trigger immediate kvcache compaction
redwoodctl runtime action --pool dedicated-us-west1-a --action kvcache-compact
```

Ada (on-call): Execute now. Morgan, coordinate deploy rollback if config alone doesn't improve in 5 minutes. Notify CustomerOps for update.

Morgan: Applying config patch. Pushing now.

DeployBot: Config patch applied at 2605001305 by eng-oncall/Morgan. Rolling to pool nodes (n=12).

Eli: Observability after config change (1m): queue_depth median dropped from 420 -> 190, p95 latency from 1600ms -> 600ms, 5xx rate from 4.2% -> 1.1%. KV eviction rate trending down after compaction.

Ada (on-call): Good improvement. Keep monitoring 10m window. If p95 remains > 800ms fallback to model-variant low-memory or drain some nodes.

CustomerOps: Notifying Acme & Finview that we have mitigations in flight — ETA 10m for stabilization. Ticket updates posted.

Eli: Note: stack traces show a hot key pattern where many requests had identical prefix keys causing large shared KV entries and eviction cascade. Root cause likely a combination of increased microbatching allowing hot prefixes to persist longer and suppressed jitter causing synchronized batch boundaries.

Zoe: Action items post-stable: (1) revert default max_microbatch_size change in v1.15.0 and instead add adaptive sizing based on queue latency, (2) add auto-trigger to disable large microbatches when kv_eviction_rate > threshold, (3) add telemetry for prefix-hotness heatmap.

Ada (on-call): Agreed. Create a JIRA for v1.15 rollback/patch and schedule follow-up postmortem. I'll stay on the channel during the stabilization window.

Morgan: We've also deployed a throttling rule to route noncritical customer traffic to spare pools to further reduce pressure.

DeployBot: Routing rule applied at 2605001500: route.noncritical -> fallback-pool-us-west1-b.

Eli: 10m check: 5xx now ~0.4%, p95 latency 420ms. KV eviction rate nominal. No further errors in Acme/Finview logs.

Ada (on-call): Great. Marking incident as mitigated. We'll keep monitoring for another 30m and then update incident record. Please add precise metrics and timelines to the incident ticket.

SRE-Triage: Incident severity downgraded from Sev2 -> Sev3 at 2605001800. Postmortem ticket: RED-INC-2026-042 created. Assigned to Zoe/Eli/Morgan.

CustomerOps: Customer notifications sent. Acme replied they see requests normalizing and appreciate the quick update.

Ada (on-call): Final notes: immediate cause = v1.15 default microbatch change + disabled jitter smoothing + hot-key traffic pattern -> KV eviction spiral -> controller queue pileup -> 5xx/latency. Live mitigations: config rollback to smaller microbatch, enabled jitter smoothing, kvcache compaction, and routing throttles. Postmortem owners: Zoe lead, Eli SRE analysis, Morgan infra changes.

Eli: I'll attach flame graphs, eviction histograms, and controller traces to the postmortem.

Zoe: I'll draft the remediation plan and timeline. Proposed hotfix: v1.15.1 with adaptive microbatch sizing and an emergency circuit-breaker if eviction_rate spikes.

Ada (on-call): Thanks everyone. Closing this thread after 30m stable window unless regressions reappear. :thumbsup:

PagerBot: Incident: mitigated (2605001800).
